headline: Draft CSRD assurance standards released; ESPR repairability consultation launched
summary: The European Commission published draft CSRD reporting assurance standards and launched an ESPR public consultation on repairability for small electricals. Unofficial reports indicate the Commission may withdraw the Green Claims Directive, while the EU Court of Justice confirmed CBAM's legal validity.

items.title: Draft CSRD assurance standards published by Commission
items.what: The European Commission published draft standards setting out criteria for mandatory third-party assurance of sustainability reporting under the CSRD.
items.meaning: As an in-scope entity from FY 2027 under post-Omnibus I rules, these standards define how auditors will evaluate your supply chain sustainability disclosures.
items.action: Review draft assurance standards to align supplier data collection processes with upcoming audit requirements.

sources.title: EU Commission Releases Draft Sustainability Reporting Assurance Standards

items.title: EU consults on ESPR repairability for small electricals
items.what: The EU launched a public consultation gathering evidence on potential repairability rules for small electrical devices under the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation.
items.meaning: Proposed repairability standards could directly impact power tool, garden equipment, and battery pack design requirements, spare part availability, and disassembly access.
items.action: Assess product portfolio repairability and consider providing feedback to the consultation.

sources.title: Public Consultation On Ecodesign Requirements On Product Repairability Under The EU ESPR

items.title: Reports suggest Green Claims Directive may be scrapped
items.what: Reports indicate the European Commission plans to abandon the proposed Green Claims Directive.
items.meaning: Specific ex-ante verification rules may not proceed, though environmental claims remain regulated under the Empowering Consumers Directive (EmpCo).
items.action: Continue auditing green claims against existing EmpCo requirements while awaiting official Commission confirmation.

sources.title: EU Commission Abandons Plans For The Green Claims Directive
European Commission plans to withdraw Green Claims Directive

items.title: EU High Court upholds CBAM legality
items.what: The EU Court of Justice rejected a legal challenge against the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism, confirming it is an environmental measure rather than a tax.
items.meaning: Although finished tool imports are currently exempt, the decision secures CBAM's legal foundation ahead of potential future extensions to downstream products.
items.action: Monitor future policy proposals regarding potential CBAM scope expansions to finished metal goods.

sources.title: EU High Court Upholds CBAM As Climate Measure, Not Tax
